headline: Profits surge as F&G turns positive; cash reserves shrink
summary_short: FNF's diluted EPS was $0.90 (+200% y/y) as consolidated revenue rose 18.2% y/y to $3,226M and net income more than doubled to $243M from $83M, while total cash fell 45% y/y to $2,467M.
summary_long: Revenue rose 18.2% y/y to $3,226M: Title revenue rose 13% to $2,004M on 16% higher closed-order volume from increased housing inventory, and F&G revenue rose 31% to $1,187M. F&G swung to a $323M pretax profit from a $26M loss a year earlier, mainly on a much smaller net derivative and reinsurance-embedded-derivative loss ($32M vs $263M). Consolidated pretax income rose to $498M from $111M; the effective tax rate rose to 35% from 26% on a deferred-tax adjustment tied to F&G's outside-basis difference. Diluted EPS was $0.90 versus $0.30. Total cash fell 45% y/y to $2,467M and shareholders' equity fell 8.1% to $7,254M; FNF repurchased $82M of stock and paid a $0.52/share dividend. No forward guidance was given.

F&G's swing from a $26M pretax loss to a $323M pretax profit is driven overwhelmingly by non-cash mark-to-market movement in derivatives and reinsurance-related embedded derivatives; this is volatility inherent to F&G's indexed-annuity hedging program, not a core-earnings improvement, and readers should discount it accordingly. drivers.explanation: Title segment revenue rose 13% on 16% higher closed-order volume driven by increased housing inventory; F&G revenue rose 31% largely on smaller net realized/unrealized investment losses.
F&G swung from a $26M pretax loss to a $323M profit as derivative and reinsurance-embedded-derivative losses shrank from $263M to $32M; Title pretax income rose on higher order volume.
Derived as pretax income plus interest expense; not separately disclosed by the company. Moves with pretax income, driven by the F&G segment's swing to profit.

Not explained via MD&A narrative; the equity statement shows a $217M other comprehensive loss, largely discount-rate remeasurement on future policy benefits and market risk benefits, contributing to the decline.

Higher Title order volume amid rising housing inventory, plus a swing to profitability in F&G's derivative and reinsurance mark-to-market results, drove the earnings increase; FNF also sold F&G Life Re for about $102M cash plus a 19.9% stake in the buyer.
